transcript:
Header: 2027-10-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SE), Marta (Harborline), Ethan (Harborline), Lisa (Harborline Sec), Noah (Harborline SRE)

Summary: quick handoff from integration PM to engineering for the joint pilot: focus areas are 1) multi-tier routing (hosted vs dedicated vs private) for customer requests via the Harborline marketplace listing, 2) cost/economic model and billing meter integration, 3) KMS and audit/log streaming for compliance. Agreed next steps and lab test window.

Topics: pilot scope, routing policy, quantization tradeoffs, KV/prefix caching, marketplace SKU bundling, billing meter mapping, SSO/KMS, rollbacks/fallback routing.

00:00:12 Jordan: thanks everyone for joining, um, quick intro - i'm Jordan from Redwood, i run partnerships for the marketplace lane, and priya here will own the perf tests and the lab runs.
00:00:25 Marta: thanks, Jordan. Marta here. we had the earlier legal and biz terms finalized, and now we want to make sure the integration is smooth from a runtime and billing perspective.
00:00:35 Priya: hi all, Priya, Redwood SE — i'll be walking through the test plan and the routing options. i also have a short deck i can drop, link will go in the notes.
00:00:46 Ethan: quick one — we care about two customer personas: small dev teams that want low-cost hosted inference, and enterprise customers that need private VPC deploys. how do we make the listing reflect both?
00:01:00 Samir: good question — we usually support multiple SKUs/variants in the marketplace listing: a hosted API SKU, a Dedicated reserved SKU, and a Private appliance SKU that points to the onprem/VPC deploy. the routing is policy-driven so the same order can map to different backend variants.
00:01:20 Marta: ok so same product but different fulfillment paths. we need the listing metadata to show latencies and expected unit costs per variant — procurement will want that.
00:01:32 Jordan: yep, we'll provide the performance profile for each variant. note though: latency numbers change with sequence length and batching. we'll include the typical 16/128/512 token profiles.
00:01:46 Lisa: on security: our compliance team insists on KMS/HSM integration and audit log forwarding. can Redwood stream audit logs to our SIEM? and support customer-managed keys?
00:02:00 Priya: yes — Redwood Private supports customer KMS via standard KMS integrations and HSM. audit logs can be forwarded via syslog/S3 hooks; we also support per-request tracing headers that Harborline can ingest. small caveat: hosted plan uses Redwood-managed KMS unless customer chooses private.
00:02:18 Noah: on the routing side, I'm concerned about cold-starts if we fall back from private to hosted — how graceful is the degrade?
00:02:28 Samir: we have automated fallback policies. if capacity in private pool is exhausted we route to a compatible quantized variant on hosted or dedicated. there will be a small latency bump; the routing policy can prefer cost or prefer latency. we can define per-route SLOs in the listing metadata.
00:02:46 Ethan: what's the quantization story? we test with int8/4-bit — how much quality reg regressions should we budget for?
00:02:55 Priya: typical tradeoff: int8 gives minimal quality drop for many decoder models; 4-bit can be riskier. we'll run an eval suite against Harborline's prompt set to measure BLEU/ROUGE or model-specific classification accuracy. caching and prefix KV reduce delta too.
00:03:14 Marta: can you clarify what the eval harness looks like? we want a reproducible repo for procurement to audit.
00:03:20 Priya: yes — we'll provide a benchmark harness: a dockerized runner that hits Redwood endpoints with annotated prompts and collects latency, token-cost, and accuracy metrics. link + README will be provided.
00:03:29 Jordan: action item: priya to drop harness link and checklist.
00:03:35 Marta: great.
00:03:40 Jordan: on billing — Harborline needs the meter mapping so your marketplace can bill per-token correctly. who owns mapping from Redwood unit to Harborline SKU?
00:03:50 Avery: (procurement) we plan to map to a per-1k-token unit for hosted/embeddings, and a flat per-hour reserved SKU for Dedicated. Private listings will be license + support.
00:04:02 Samir: Redwood provides a metering webhook and usage-export CSV. we can push a sample file and the naming convention (model_id, variant, tokens, customer_id, timestamp). you can ingest that into your billing pipeline.
00:04:15 Ethan: any gotchas on timezone and decimal rounding? our billing engine expects ISO timestamps and microbilling decimals.
00:04:22 Samir: we emit ISO-8601 timestamps in UTC and tokens rounded to integer counts. for microbilling we can emit token fractions via the usage-export if needed — it's configurable.
00:04:35 Lisa: one more security check — responsibility for PII in prompts. Hosted is shared infrastructure; if enterprise requires data not leave their VPC, we must use Private. is that accurate?
00:04:46 Priya: correct — hosted is multi-tenant; we have data retention controls and redaction but for regulated data Private is the recommended approach. we'll document retention windows in the listing.
00:04:58 Marta: next: latency tests. Noah and Priya — can you sketch the lab plan?
00:05:06 Priya: sure. plan A: run three waveforms — steady low-rps (10 rps), burst (100 rps), and long-context sessions (2k tokens). measure p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, KV hit rates. we will test three backend variants: hosted-optim, dedicated-1x-reserve, and private-small.
00:05:27 Noah: we'll stand up harborline test harness in our lab and provide access to a subnet. can Redwood run the ephemeral dedicated nodes for the tests?
00:05:36 Samir: yes — we can spin dedicated nodes in our sandbox for the window. cost for that will be covered under the pilot credits we agreed in the partner MOU.
00:05:46 Ethan: about the KV/prefix cache — we use a lot of conversation state. will cache locality across clients affect billing?
00:05:55 Priya: caching reduces token generation and cost but we still meter compute spent on new tokens. we'll show token delta pre/post cache. for conversations we recommend prefix caching at the route-level.
00:06:08 Marta: on the marketplace listing UI — we need to show clear fallback behavior and SLA language. can Redwood provide default wording?
00:06:16 Jordan: yes, we'll propose copy and an operations SLA snippet. you'll have legal signoff on the phraseology.
00:06:24 Lisa: on encryption — we need envelope encryption and key rotation support. Redwood's key-rotation window?
00:06:31 Priya: we support rotation via KMS with no downtime if keys are in KMS; rotation is managed by customer KMS schedule. for Redwood-managed KMS rotation is quarterly by default.
00:06:41 Marta: procurement wants the pricing band for hosted so they can show in RFx. Jordan, can you send the price matrix?
00:06:48 Jordan: yes — i'll send the partner pricing matrix. note: these are pilot rates and can change slightly at GA.
00:06:56 Avery: tie to action item: Jordan to circulate pricing assumptions and partner playbook.
00:07:02 Jordan: noted.
00:07:10 Ethan: technical deep dive: network egress costs. if we route between regions, who pays the cross-region egress?
00:07:18 Samir: egress depends on deployment mode. Hosted: Redwood covers egress inside our cloud allowances for pilot; Dedicated and Private: customer covers egress from their VPCs. we'll put a callout in the listing.
00:07:33 Noah: also want to test go/no-go for onprem appliance style deployment. what's the expected onboarding time?
00:07:39 Priya: for our onprem appliance we have a pre-built helm chart — typical onboarding 2-4 weeks depending on networking and KMS. for the pilot we'll do a light-weight registry/airgap skip test to validate telemetry.
00:07:52 Marta: two sticky items: 1) marketplace SKU taxonomy mapping, 2) billing reconciliation cadence. how often can we get metering files? daily? hourly?
00:07:59 Samir: metering files can be emitted hourly or daily. for the pilot we recommend hourly to catch edge cases; production could be daily aggregates.
00:08:10 Lisa: audit logs — retention timeframe and format?
00:08:14 Priya: we support S3 exports and event streaming to your SIEM; retention configurable up to 365 days on Private; hosted default is 30 days.
00:08:24 Marta: ok, any blockers?
00:08:27 Ethan: i want to validate the quant-quality matrix. can't overpromise quality drop.
00:08:31 Priya: understood — we'll include the eval report per quant profile.
00:08:36 Jordan: let's recap next steps and owners. Priya to drop harness link and perf plan by 11/2. Ethan to share billing sample by 11/5. Lisa to collate SOC2/KMS notes by 11/4. Jordan to share pricing matrix by 10/31. schedule lab window week of 11/8 — Noah and Priya to coordinate.
00:09:05 Marta: thanks — sounds good. any other questions?
00:09:10 Noah: one last: do we have a recommended default routing policy for marketplace listings? like prefer latency for enterprise, cost for small dev?
00:09:18 Samir: yes — we have policy templates: "latency-first", "cost-first", "balanced". we'll include those and a short decision table for Harborline.
00:09:27 Jordan: perfect. we'll send links and close the loop. thanks all.

Crosstalk and mumbled wrap up ~ last 2 minutes, minor audio glitches.

References shared in chat: link: /playbooks/harborline-pilot-harness.tar.gz, link: /docs/partner-listing-playbook-v2.pdf, spreadsheet: harborline-billing-sample.csv
